title: 1991 Biagini Passo

highlights: Extremely rare Biagini Passo, believed to be the only example in the US
Unique Mk1 Golf Cabriolet body with Mk2 Golf Country Syncro AWD drivetrain
Recaro front seats in blue Alcantara with Nardi steering wheel
red_flags: Seller disclosed complete brake failure after upholstery shop visit, requiring new master cylinder and proportioning valve
Rear drum brake parts from Golf Country and Passat did not fit, indicating unresolved parts/compatibility issue
Auction withdrawn by BaT mid-sale due to seller's mechanical issues
normalized.prelim_summary: This one-of-a-kind Biagini Passo—a coachbuilt Syncro AWD cabriolet based on VW Golf components—was being bid to $12,500 before the seller pulled it after a brake failure during servicing. The car is mechanically compromised as disclosed and was withdrawn pending repairs, so a buyer should wait for a relisting with resolved brakes before bidding seriously.

critical_evidence.evidence: The car came from Austria to the US in the early 2020s and carries a Connecticut title. No prior CA registration, CARB/BAR referee determination, HS-7/EPA 3520-1 forms or emissions label are mentioned.
The listing names the Syncro AWD system but gives no tight-turn test, rear-drive engagement check, viscous coupling condition, or transaxle/angle drive/rear drive fluid receipts.

One lift photo shows the front subframe, steering rack and exhaust with surface corrosion on the exhaust. There are no photos of the floors with carpets lifted, sills, A-pillar bases, arches behind the flares, or subframe mounts. Additional gallery images were not examined here.

The listing states the master cylinder, proportioning valve and rear shoes were replaced. The seller comment adds a Techtonics Tuning rear prop valve and says 'I'll post a pic of the Repair Order soon'. No RO or post-repair road-test report is posted. The prior listing noted Golf Country/Passat rear drum parts did not fit.
No timing belt or water pump date or receipt is mentioned. The single Carfax entry (October 2026 service) is not itemised in the listing.

documentation.rationale: Identity half is partial: chassis number, a CT title (brand not stated) and a one-entry Carfax. Maintenance half is essentially absent: no timing belt, driveline fluid or import/emissions paperwork, and the brake RO is promised, not posted.

condition.rationale: Photos show a cosmetically tidy car with a fresh-looking interior and A/T tires. Against that, the seller disclosed a brake failure on the drive back from the upholstery shop, followed by master cylinder, aftermarket prop valve and rear drum work with no repair order. Surface rust is visible on the front lock carrier, and the structure and Syncro health are unshown.

price_value.rationale: No fair value estimate and no sold comps. The $3,800 no-reserve bid is early, and the withdrawn listing reached about $12,500. Any hammer price carries the risk that the car cannot be registered in California, which would make it near-worthless for Jason's use regardless of price.

mission_fit.rationale: Manual and full of character, but 89 hp, a 35-year-old Syncro driveline with unobtainable body parts, a thin resale market and an unproven CA registration path conflict with 'reliable, inspectable, easy to resell in 6-24 months'.

logistics.rationale: Located in Illinois as a remote timed auction. PPI access is unstated with under five days to close, and CA registration/smog feasibility for a non-certified import is unknown and possibly costly.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: A genuinely rare coachbuilt manual Syncro cabriolet with period Recaros and Nardi wheel. Tempered by aftermarket wheels and graphics and by the fact that it is a slow soft-roader rather than the driver's roadster the brief centres on.

ppi_focus: Brake system: master cylinder, aftermarket rear proportioning valve installation, rear drum fitment and adjustment, line condition, and a road test for front/rear balance and pull
Syncro: tight-turn binding/crow-hop test, rear drive engagement with one rear wheel raised, viscous coupling and freewheel behaviour
Angle drive and rear final drive leaks and whine; propshaft centre bearing and couplers for vibration at 40–60 mph
Biagini subframe welds, mounting points and any crush damage; CV boots and joints at the lifted angles
Cabriolet structure: floors under the carpets, sills, A-pillar/windshield base, strut towers, battery tray, roll bar base, arches behind the flares
Front lock carrier rust seen in the engine-bay photo; cooling flanges, hoses and radiator
Timing belt condition and date marks, oil leaks at the valve cover, cam and crank seals
Emissions hardware present (catalyst, O2 sensor) and engine code, to assess the CA smog/CARB path
Soft top frame, the new zippered rear panel, and the tailgate seal for water ingress
what_would_change_verdict: Documented proof that the car can be registered and smog-passed in California (prior CA registration or a CARB/BAR determination) would remove the dominant risk.
A posted itemised brake RO plus a PPI confirming the brake balance and a healthy Syncro driveline would lift the condition rating.
Carpets-up underside photos showing solid floors and sills would lift both condition and documentation.
Evidence that CA registration requires CARB-lab certification or is not possible, a refused PPI, or structural rust found under the carpets would move it sharply down.
evidence.mission_note: It satisfies 'manual with a point of view' but fails the bridge brief's practical tests: a reliable, easy-to-resell car with a proven path to CA registration. It is a novelty purchase, not a pragmatic bridge.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes the identity basics: a chassis number, a five-speed Syncro drivetrain, a Connecticut title, and a one-entry Carfax with 31,204 last reported. The photos show a cosmetically tidy car with the Biagini-unique body parts apparently present. Observed problems include a disclosed brake failure that led to a new master cylinder, an aftermarket Techtonics rear proportioning valve and rear drums, after the prior listing noted ill-fitting rear drum parts. The repair order for that work is promised but not posted. Surface rust is visible on the front lock carrier, and two exterior photos appear to show silver wheels on the far side. None of the five model-critical items is satisfied. There is no California registration evidence for a non-US-certified European import, no Syncro driveline test or fluid records, no carpets-up rust photos, and no timing belt receipt. The California emissions and registration question outweighs everything else, because without a clear path the car cannot serve as Jason's daily second car in Carmel. PPI access before the no-reserve close in about five days is unconfirmed.
evidence.next_action: Before Monday, message the seller asking for the import documents (HS-7, EPA 3520-1), any California registration or CARB history, the itemised brake repair order, and permission for a third-party PPI in La Grange before the auction closes.
